extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, political reformers, and students of public administration
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive principles and institutional design criteria for reorganizing state and municipal governments to increase efficiency, responsibility, and capacity for social reform. Covers executive structure, electoral design, policing, justice, education, municipal home rule, and the proper division of national vs. state power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency requires authority and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no efficiency without responsibility. There can be no responsibility without authority. The authority and responsibility residing ultimately in the people must be delegated; and it must not be emasculated in the process of delegation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation must give public officials real power to act and simultaneously make them accountable so the people can fix offenses and punish offenders. Anti-pattern: stripping delegated authority to avoid potential misuse, producing inefficiency and lack of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executives must have full powers but be recallable and punishable
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive shall have full power to do either well or ill, but if he does do ill, he will have no defense against punishment. Chief executive elected for a comparatively long term, and subject to recall under certain defined conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine extended tenure (to allow effective administration) with recall mechanisms so voters can remove incompetent or corrupt executives. This balances authority for action with political responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive-led cabinet (executive council) appointed by chief executive
rubrics_metrics.description: He would be surrounded by an executive council, similar to the President's Cabinet, appointed by himself and consisting of a Controller, Attorney General, Secretary of State, Commissioner of Public Works, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Councilors are expected to share the chief's essential public policy views and to be responsible for particular departments; they work through permanent departmental chiefs. This concentrates executive responsibility and aligns administrative leadership with policy direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief executive power to introduce legislation and appeal to electorate
rubrics_metrics.description: He shall have the additional power of introducing legislation into a legislative council and, in case his proposed legislation were rejected or amended in an inacceptable manner, of appealing to the electorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the executive initiative in lawmaking and a democratic check (appeal to voters) against uncooperative legislatures. Ensures executive accountability while enabling policy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative council design: large districts, cumulative voting, limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislative council would be elected from large districts and, if possible, by some cumulative system of voting. They ... might be subject to recall. They would have the power ... of authorizing the appropriation of public money and, also, of passing on certain minor classes of legislation--closely associated with administrative functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the council to fiscal authorization and minor legislation; require express popular approval for substantial legislation. Use larger districts and voting systems that promote broader representation and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular approval required for substantial legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: But in relation to all legislation of substantial importance express popular approval would be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve major policy changes for measures that obtain explicit popular consent (e.g., referendum/plebiscite), preventing small representative bodies from imposing sweeping changes without direct mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive authority to remove and appoint administrative officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief executive should possess the power of removing any administrative official in the employ of the state and of appointing a successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables the executive to ensure departmental leadership aligns with policy; but permanent departmental chiefs (experts) should exercise operational control subject to this executive oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use permanent, expert departmental chiefs (not fixed-period turnover)
rubrics_metrics.description: His several councilors would be executive officials, responsible for particular departments of the public service; but they would exercise their authority through permanent departmental chiefs ... they would not be changed at fixed periods or for irrelevant reasons. They would be just as permanent or as transient as the good of the service demanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor professional permanence and technical mastery in departmental leadership; appointments should be stable insofar as service needs demand, avoiding politicized periodic turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate authority to reduce the need for professional politicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the number of elective officials. Under the proposed method of organization the number of elections and the number of men to be elected would be comparatively few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By limiting elective offices (voter casts ballots only for a few key positions), diminish the market for political specialists whose livelihood depends on numerous elections. Anti-pattern: proliferation of elective posts that sustain machines and corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify government so voters face only decisive choices
rubrics_metrics.description: A democracy has no interest in making good government complicated, difficult, and costly. ... Only decisive decisions and choices are submitted to the voter. The cost of government in time, ability, training, and energy should fall not upon the followers but upon the leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design electoral and administrative systems that avoid overwhelming voters with frequent, complex ballots; concentrate technical burdens on leaders so voters can exercise meaningful oversight without fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about secret ballot and direct primaries as sole reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: The secret Australian ballot ... has not diminished the personal and partisan allegiance ... The system of direct primaries ... may in the long run merely emphasize the evil which it is intended to abate ... the number of elections will be very much increased ... the politicians can easily nominate their own candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these devices as limited tools. They can help in some contexts but may exacerbate problems if not accompanied by institutional redesign (e.g., reducing elective offices). Beware mechanical fixes that increase electoral complexity and opportunities for political machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: State constabulary for maintaining order and preventing lynching
rubrics_metrics.description: A state government ... would necessarily demand from the people a police force which was really capable of keeping the peace. It would need a state constabulary, subject to its control and numerous enough for all ordinary emergencies. Such bodies ... could gradually stamp out lynch law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a well-trained, disciplined, quickly deployable force under state (not local) control to handle strikes, mob violence, and to protect vulnerable populations from local majoritarian abuses. Local sheriffs/militia are insufficient due to local bias or slowness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speedy and certain administration of criminal justice
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-informed state government would also necessarily recognize the intimate connection between the prevention of lynching and the speedy and certain administration of criminal justice. It would seek not merely to stamp out disorder, but to anticipate it by doing away with the substantial injustice wrought by the procedure of the great majority of American criminal courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize procedural reforms that ensure swift, reliable justice to deter violence and prevent miscarriages that provoke disorder. Avoid systems that over-protect procedural interests at the expense of collective safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform penitentiaries, reformatories, and insane asylums toward rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The machinery and the management [of penitentiaries, reformatories, and insane asylums] are capable of considerable improvement. The steady increase both of crime and insanity is demanding ... separating out those criminals and feeble-minded people who are capable of being restored to the class of useful citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should modernize institutions to emphasize rehabilitation and reintegration where possible, and to consider preventive measures addressing social determinants of crime and insanity. Anti-pattern: neglect and uneven quality across states.

rubrics_metrics.name: State competence over education with purpose-driven training
rubrics_metrics.description: The educational system of the country, which should remain under exclusive state jurisdiction, is well adapted to the extremely complicated purpose of endowing its various pupils with the general and special training most helpful to the creation of genuine individuals, useful public servants, and loyal and contented citizens of their own states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should design education policy to develop individual capacities and civic competence. Although many states show good will, poor organization undermines outcomes, so administrative reform is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: States as laboratories: experiment, emulation, and inter-state cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: No better machinery for the accomplishment of a progressive programme of social reform could be advised than a collection of governments endowed with the powers of an American state, and really desirous of advancing particular social questions towards their solution. Such a system would be flexible; it would provoke emulation; it would encourage initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use state-level policy experimentation with the expectation of adjusting or withdrawing reforms based on results; facilitate comparison and consultation (e.g., a 'House of Governors') rather than enforcing uniform national policies prematurely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee municipal home rule for economic and business matters
rubrics_metrics.description: A politically regenerated state would guarantee in its constitution a much larger measure of home rule to the cities ... the functions delegated or preserved should so far as possible be completely delegated or preserved. ... the city as an economic and business organism should be left pretty much to its own devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State constitutions should protect municipal autonomy over local economic decisions and public service franchises; retain state oversight only for essential functions (order and education). Anti-pattern: intrusive state supervision that undermines local economic responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service corporations controlling municipal franchises subject to municipal jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service corporations which control franchises in cities ... should be subject, consequently, to municipal jurisdiction and only that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localities that bear the benefits and costs of municipal franchises should have primary regulatory authority; avoid deflecting municipal economic governance to distant state regulators when impacts are local.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central government should handle commerce, corporate control, wealth distribution, and poverty prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation of commerce, the control of corporations, and the still more radical questions connected with the distribution of wealth and the prevention of poverty--questions of this kind should be left exclusively to the central government; or ... the states should exercise such jurisdiction as the agents of the central government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve issues of national economic scope for federal authority because states lack the necessary power and independence; otherwise state efforts will be diverted and national policy will be inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-state commerce distinction obstructs effective national industrial policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinction between domestic and inter-state commerce which is implied by the Constitutional distribution of powers is a distinction of insignificant economic or industrial importance; and its necessary legal enforcement makes the carrying out of an efficient national industrial policy almost impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that corporations operate as integrated entities across state lines; fragmented state regulation produces conflicting compartments and incentivizes corruption. Effective regulation requires national-level authority to avoid contradictory state rules that undermine both public interest and corporate stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer state-level institutional experimentation over wholesale Federal constitutional amendment (with one key exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation cannot afford to experiment with its fundamental law as it may and must experiment with its local institutions. ... The Federal Constitution is very much less in need of amendment than are those of the several states. ... This exception is, however, of the utmost importance: the inter-state commerce clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hasty federal constitutional changes; pursue reform at state/local levels first. Exception: consider federal constitutional action where the inter-state commerce clause prevents effective national economic regulation.
